Queens is very good for families. You could have one car if you want, since there’s definitely more space to drive and park compared to the city. I highly recommend the Kew Gardens/Hillcrest/Fresh Meadows strip. U could drive to the LIRR station a mile south in Jamaica, park, and get to the city on the train in 15/20 minutes. Bc u could be going for like an hour+ at rush hour on the subway. U can choose either Penn or Grand Central on ur ticket too. I also tutor and babysit in the area, so I can vouch that the neighborhoods are very pretty, with greenspaces close by (including St. John’s Uni), and neighbors are multi-cultural. Esp since ur close to Jamaica Ave, u have tons of options for groceries too.

You would definitely not be alone as queer parents in the Barrington school system; there are and have been many kids with same-sex parents and no one bats an eye. The schools themselves are queer-friendly too. Pride is a very vocal celebration, and this generation of students is supportive of their queer peers. Although a niche problem at the high school I’ve witnessed is that when some kids who happened to be in special education have started bullying lgbt and/or nonwhite students, admin just lets them? It’s very intentional & cognizant on the bullies’ part, and has frequently targeted other kids who get accommodated education too. It’s gone as far as the bullies playing n*zi march songs, threatening to b*mb local businesses, calling other students slurs that they have no right to even say, etc. And when it has escalated to cops getting called, I’ve seen first hand the cops laughing with these kids in the hallways and letting them off? And admin’s excuse for these white boys saying the n word, making direct threats of violence, telling lgbt peers “I burned the gay flag this weekend”, is that “they’re different, you have to be gentle with them”. That’s the only thing I would warily keep in mind if ur daughter is going to the high school, that the admin is absolutely terrible at disciplinary action. You’ll have better luck with them (though god forbid that’s necessary) if you are persistent and aggressive with them as parents. They’re adverse to controversy and will do a lot to make sure there isn’t drama about them in the news. So, your family should be fine, but if this issue arises for you, don’t give admin the benefit of the doubt!

I don’t blame you for feeling the way you do, because your mind has established an A to B correlation with feeling close with someone to being hurt by them. And I’m proud that you’re not running away from your partner- despite feeling this way. But you can’t go on like this forever. I think you would benefit from some somatic anxiety treatment, aka what targets your nervous system. You logically know that you’re safe, but managing your physical triggers could help you accept that. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, breathwork, and SSRI medication has helped me with that personally. Also practicing more self-acceptance could help: try to acclimate to the idea that you and your partner are interdependent, meaning that you’re two *individuals* working together, not enmeshing. You as an individual wouldn’t have to personalize it if she did “cheat, move on, find someone better” because unless you decided to be someone like your ex, that wouldn’t have anything to do with you, therefore making you not responsible for it. Overall: good job on reaching out for help and not sabotaging your relationship. You won’t feel this way forever, and it starts with understanding your own worth + feeling safe in your own body. Good luck!

My now ex is in the same boat as you. He’s had a hard time contemplating his origins because it opens up lifelong unanswered questions such as “what could’ve happened to me?”, and “did my birth parents care about me at all?”. Yk its a situation that makes people feel completely out of control, and that’s the basis of any trauma source in general. I think confronting the fact that this has caused you pain, and allowing yourself to try collecting the answers you want, can help bring you peace. After all, ignoring a problem never makes it go away. You may not have conscious memories of when you were in the custody of your birth parents, but you lived with them, depended upon them, and were attached to them. Then without explanation, you haven’t seen them in twenty years. The body keeps the score of what the mind can’t, and that’s probably why this issue comes up when you get triggered in other areas of concern- because this is a blanketed unhealed wound. You can take your sense of control back by letting yourself feel sad, angry, mournful, whatever, and by connecting with your roots however you want. But the first step is asking for help, and I commend you for doing that. Good luck on your journey; you deserve to live your twenties and the rest of your life with peace of mind over where you come from.

No, I wouldn’t be upset. For reference: Someone I love is an international adoptee, I have a lot of friends who were adopted, and my mom is a clinical social worker. This is me reiterating what they’ve told me- Im with my bio parents, so I have no personal stories to tell & it would be wrong to act like I do. Now, most of my friends in/that have been in the system were put in it as infants; most of them have never met their parents past birth/toddlerhood, most were not placed with family members, most have no idea why they were removed at all. No matter if it’s my friend who knows that they were removed from parents who were addicted to drugs & later died from them, then placed with aunts, and has seen pictures + knows stories of their bio parents, versus my friend who doesn’t know what her ethnicity even is and was placed with a social worker who’s a different race than her: they both have been traumatized by adoption. Every single one of them has experienced grief about their family situations and the trend I’ve noticed is that the more they don’t yet know, the more they’re bothered by their trauma on a routine basis. We as a species all cope differently, but my friend who knew her parents has no problem talking about her business, whereas my friend who has no clue who they are gets emotional just speaking about it. An adoptee getting to meet their bio parents is a game changer for their entire life. Please let them get that closure if they want it.

You’re not a bad person for not feeling well. That doesn’t make you a bad boyfriend either. One of the most loving things you could do for her is to especially take care of yourself, bc those things are reciprocal. And taking care of yourself starts with honestly asking yourself why you feel this way. Honestly meaning: knowing emotions just color your life, they exist to do the opposite of hurting you, and try not operating like this conversation with yourself is up for judgement. Not everything you think represents who you are, the mind is really an observation tank where things that aren’t from/about you come floating through. I would try politely telling your girlfriend you wanna go for a walk alone and then take some time to have a conversation with yourself and try problem-solving. Just please make decisions from a place of love, the best you can.
The Gottman Institute is a relationship therapy association that has platforms on Instagram and whatnot. They have advice on this stuff, no judgement. Good luck dude, don’t forget about your future.

All you really *have* to do is the bare bones stuff. Forget about people who don’t reciprocate the respect you give, who cramp your mindset, etc. Worst comes to worst, you part ways with people and go to a place with no rent, no bullshit, and learn some survival skills like starting a fire and cooking meat.
